title: proactive reclaim + prefetch block allocator to reduce tail latency under bursty KV workloads
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduce a proactive block allocator with background reclaim and prefetch heuristics for the paged KV cache. Improves p99 tail latency under bursty workloads; opt-in via config. No API changes.
description:
Context & motivation: production workloads show frequent short-lived bursts (chat multiplexer fan-out, streaming completions) that create temporary KV cache pressure. Under those patterns the paged block allocator can stall on synchronous evictions and cold reads, producing p99 latency spikes. This PR implements a proactive reclaim + prefetch path in the block allocator and ties it into the request scheduler so hot-path requests can pre-warm adjacent blocks instead of blocking on synchronous allocations.

What this PR does (high level): single continuous description of changes: added a background reclaim worker that tracks a lightweight hotset, heuristically reclaims low-utility blocks during idle CPU cycles, and issues async prefetches when a request accesses a prefix that suggests near-future access (sequence-aware prefetch). The allocator exposes two knobs: reclaim_budget and prefetch_threshold. We wire allocator events into the continuous batching scheduler so that batches containing "fast-path" tokens can trigger immediate prefetch of the next chunks, reducing synchronous page faults. The design favors bounded background work and cooperative prefetch to avoid increased GPU stalls.

Key design points: 1) Epoch-based reuse counters: reduce contention by only promoting reuse candidates at epoch boundaries (cheap atomic counters). 2) Hotset detector: probabilistic LRU sketch that feeds reclaim priorities; tiny memory overhead. 3) Async prefetch: non-blocking I/O to warm KV pages on host or NVMe before kernel hot path needs them. 4) Scheduler integration: a request tag "fast-path-prefetch" is added by the runtime when continuous batching predicts short next-token windows. 5) Safety: reclaim never frees blocks in use (pin-bit + epoch); prefetch is best-effort and fails silently.

Performance summary (canary & lab): microbench with synthetic bursty fanout (100ms bursts, 10x QPS): p99 latency reduced from ~210ms to ~120ms on our standard benchmark rig; median unchanged. End-to-end RL workload (multiplexed chat) showed 38% fewer synchronous allocation stalls and 7% lower token CPU cost due to fewer kernel re-compiles from miss patterns. Canary across 10 customers for a week: no regressions, average request error rate unchanged.

Backward compatibility & rollout: opt-in feature flag allocator.mode=proactive; default off for release build. Gradual rollout plan included in the PR: feature gated, mobile canary, then platform-wide release. No external API changes.

Test plan: unit tests for reclaim worker, hotset sketch, and epoch reuse; integration test that simulates prefetch race and ensures no double-free; end-to-end perf test added to perf-canary suite. CI includes deterministic allocator fuzz harness.

Files changed (high level): implemented new allocator core (runtime/kv/block_allocator/proactive_allocator.{cc,h}), hotset sketch (runtime/kv/hotset_sketch.h), scheduler hooks (runtime/scheduler/prefetch_integration.cc), config bindings and docs (docs/allocator.md), tests (tests/kv/proactive_reclaim_test.cc, tests/kv/prefetch_integration_test.cc), and updates to perf-canary configs.

Short code/config snippet (illustrative): allocator:
  mode: proactive
  reclaim_budget: 32  # max blocks reclaimed per idle epoch
  prefetch_threshold: 0.25  # fraction of hotset hit probability that triggers prefetch

Edge cases and mitigations: 1) noisy tenants: sketch adapts decay rate per tenant; heavy noisy traffic yields lower prefetch aggressiveness. 2) NVMe-backed stores: prefetch has backpressure and is capped by prefetch_budget to avoid I/O queuing. 3) Memory storms: background reclaim is throttled when memory pressure crosses a configured watermark.

Commit summary (see commits/ below): initial implementation + unit tests; hotset sketch; scheduler hook; add config bindings; integration tests; perf tweaks and CI fixes; docs and release notes.

Review & approvals: reviewers requested clarifications on reuse semantics (answered: epoch decouples pin lifetime from immediate reuse) and on what happens during host OOM (answered: reclaim will be opportunistic but never evict pinned blocks). Performance owner asked for microbench plots; attached results. After two rounds of feedback and a small refactor to reduce allocator lock contention, reviewers approved.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after CI passed.

Why this is different from previous allocator work: previous PRs focused on compacting or reusing freed blocks in-place and softpin heuristics. This change is behaviorally different: it proactively reclaims during idle windows and prefetches predicted pages, which reduces synchronous blocking on first access and complements reuse/pin improvements.

Monitoring & rollout notes: added allocator.reclaim.rate and allocator.prefetch.hits metrics and dashboard tile. Alert: reclaim_rate_drop -> investigation. Canary showed stable reclaim_rate ~20-30 blocks/s on typical medium workloads.

Follow-ups: 1) experimental cross-tenant prefetch global budget, 2) GPU-side prefetch hints to the kernel for faster device-side warming, 3) quantized prefetch prioritization for embd-heavy workloads.
